notes: RS-25 sea level, 15 deg cone (before): over the settled window (steps 6000-12000, nd time 47.14-92.87) mass flow 474.7 kg/s mean (range 267.9-759.8), C_f 1.8094 mean (range 1.6957-1.8897), residual 2.18e-2 at the end, converged false, confidence NotConverged (253 x 415 cells, Compact plume, floors 665). THE WINDOW IS A LIMIT CYCLE, not a steady state — see the rs25-sea-level-unsteady note.

RS-25 sea level, 80% bell (after): over the settled window (steps 6000-12000, nd time 42.70-84.56) mass flow 338.8 kg/s mean (range 3.4-469.2), C_f 1.6263 mean (range 1.4780-1.8512), residual 6.21e-2 at the end, converged false, confidence NotConverged (224 x 415 cells, Compact plume, floors 0). THE WINDOW IS A LIMIT CYCLE, not a steady state — see the rs25-sea-level-unsteady note.

RS-25 at sea level is overexpanded (p_e/p_a ~ 0.21 at the preset's gamma 1.20 — quasi-1D p_e ~ 21.6 kPa against 101.3 kPa ambient, below the 0.40 separation threshold, the SS13 separation-warning regime) and has NO steady state in this inviscid model: a 30k-step probe of both contours shows the shock system breathing in and out of the nozzle, with exit-plane readouts oscillating over mdot 291-738 kg/s (cone) / 48-895 (bell), exit Mach 0.58-2.97 / 0.77-3.59, C_f 1.41-1.86 / 1.43-1.79. The cone-vs-bell C_f comparison is therefore asserted at 20 km (attached flow), not at sea level.

RS-25 at 20 km, 15 deg cone (before): over the settled window (steps 6000-12000, nd time 36.48-70.79) mass flow 489.6 kg/s mean, C_f 1.6667 mean (range 1.6549-1.6780, half-window drift +0.0007), residual 1.14e-2 at the end (11x RESIDUAL_CONVERGED = 1e-3), converged false, confidence NotConverged (253 x 415 cells, Compact plume, floors 1495).

RS-25 at 20 km, 80% bell (after): over the settled window (steps 6000-12000, nd time 34.60-66.60) mass flow 490.7 kg/s mean, C_f 1.6858 mean (range 1.6763-1.6939, half-window drift +0.0009), residual 7.17e-3 at the end (7x RESIDUAL_CONVERGED = 1e-3), converged false, confidence NotConverged (224 x 415 cells, Compact plume, floors 0).

NEITHER 20 km run converges, and nothing here is asserted as if it did: at step 12000 the residual is 1.14e-2 (cone) / 7.17e-3 (bell) against RESIDUAL_CONVERGED = 1e-3 — 11x / 7x above it — StepInfo.converged is false for both and every Report carries Confidence::NotConverged. What IS asserted is the mean over the declared settled window (steps 6000-12000, nd time 36.48-70.79), qualified first by a time-based steadiness check on the same window: C_f half-window drift 0.0007 / 0.0009 (cone/bell) against a cone-to-bell difference of 0.0191, and residual second-half/first-half 0.55 / 0.56. The single-instant version of this assert read +0.0218 at step 5511 and NEGATIVE before step ~2000 — it was a snapshot of a wobble.

Raptor 2 is NOT routed through the Rao table. Published geometry (FAA Analysis Report 2019-001b Table 1): theta_n 32.0 deg, theta_e 6.0 deg, downstream throat arc 0.300 R_t (the Rao/TOP construction's 0.382 R_t does not apply). At eps 34.3 the table matches theta_n at 0.750 (0.00 deg off) but theta_e is 3.64 deg off there, and the percent minimising the WORSE of the two angles (0.821) still misses by 1.85 deg — no bell percent satisfies both, so the table cannot represent this engine. This is a contour-family mismatch, NOT a gamma effect: Rao (1958) states gamma barely moves the contour at fixed length and area ratio, and the sign is inverted (gamma 1.16 vs the chart's ~1.23 makes the exit angle larger, worth under 0.7 deg). The app now takes the two angles directly (ContourKind::DirectBell); 76% remains the LENGTH only.
